result.question: How do leading agentic-AI companies and agencies position, message, and convert on their websites — and what should a small African "Agent as a System" studio borrow? Specifically: (1) Positioning & copy: exact headline/subheadline patterns, section order, and CTA language used by LangChain, CrewAI, Lindy, Sierra AI, Decagon, Cognition (Devin), Relevance AI, and custom-AI-agent agencies/studios selling to SMBs (including any called "Hyperagents" or similar); how they explain "AI agents" to non-technical business buyers; how they present use cases and case studies. (2) Market gap: how agentic AI is being sold to African/Nigerian SMBs, WhatsApp-first agent products, and what messaging gaps exist for operations-focused (farm, hospitality/venue) businesses. (3) Assessment-led conversion: "AI readiness assessment" / "agent readiness" scoring frameworks used by consultancies (McKinsey, BCG, Deloitte, smaller agencies) — what 5-8 short questions best predict a business's readiness for AI agents (dimensions like process documentation, data digitization, volume of repetitive tasks, staff structure, existing tools), and how score tiers are typically labeled and presented. (4) Conversion patterns: evidence on quiz/assessment lead magnets vs contact forms for B2B services conversion. Deliver: concrete copy formulas and vocabulary that works (and what to avoid), a recommended 5-7 question readiness quiz with scoring weights and tier labels, and a recommended page section order for a consultation-led customer journey.
result.summary: Leading agentic-AI companies sell agents with outcome-and-metaphor headlines ("The AI concierge for every customer"; "AI agents that drive business impact, managed by your team"), explain the technology through plain-language work framings (playbooks your experts design and agents execute; role/goal/instructions; "digital sidekick"/"partner in your growth"), prove value with one-line named-customer metrics rather than narrative case studies, and convert via demo-led or dual (free-trial + talk-to-sales) CTAs — none of the product companies studied use assessment lead magnets, which is exactly the gap an assessment-led studio can occupy. The assessment-led pattern is well developed by consultancies: Cisco's AI Readiness Index (6 weighted pillars, 49 indicators, graded 0/25-50/100 deployment-maturity scoring, four named tiers with explicit cutoffs) and BridgeView IT's SMB quiz (5 pillars, 5-minute promise, "no technical prep required," instant report → Schedule a Consultation) together provide a complete template, and Interact's platform data shows service-provider quizzes convert 42.2% of starters into leads. For an African "Agent as a System" studio, the recommended formula is: metaphor/outcome hero + verb-triad subheadline, plain-language agent explanation using partner/division-of-labor vocabulary, industry-specific use cases (farm, venue, hospitality) with quantified proof, a 7-question readiness quiz scored on graded maturity across process documentation, data digitization, task volume, tools, team, ownership, and risk, feeding a tiered instant report into a consultation CTA. One urgent market fact: Meta's free, WhatsApp-native Business Agent launched globally in June 2026, so a WhatsApp-first studio must position above it — custom multi-step operational agents and systems, not basic chat replies.

findings.claim: Hero headline pattern: winning agentic-AI homepages lead with a business metaphor or outcome plus human control — never the technology. Decagon: 'The AI concierge for every customer' with the Build/Optimize/Scale verb-triad subheadline ('Build, optimize, and scale AI agents that treat every customer like the only one'); Relevance AI: 'AI agents that drive business impact, managed by your team' with a named buyer segment (GTM teams) in the subheadline; Torq: trademarked product name + one-line capability ('Bespoke AI Agents that can drive any security process'). Reusable formulas: '[Metaphor role] for every [customer type]' and 'AI agents that [outcome], managed by your team' — the human-oversight clause doubles as trust messaging.
findings.evidence: All three heroes verified verbatim by live fetch on 2026-07-03; unanimous 3-0 verification on Decagon and Relevance claims. None of the heroes contain LLM/architecture language.

findings.claim: Explaining 'AI agents' to non-technical buyers: the consistent vocabulary is work-relationship framing, not technology. Decagon frames configuration as natural-language 'Agent Operating Procedures' — writing workflows in plain language with 'greater transparency and trusted results'; Relevance AI uses division-of-labor ('Your domain experts design the playbooks. Your agents execute them autonomously. Together, they scale what used to take entire teams'); Torq uses 'give them a role, a goal, and clear declarative instructions' and stresses transparency/control over autonomy ('a dial, not a switch'); Salesforce defines an SMB agent as 'an intelligent technology partner that handles routine tasks' and a 'digital sidekick' — 'more than just a tool, a partner in your growth'. Vocabulary to use: partner, sidekick, playbook, handles routine tasks, your team stays in control, shows its work. Vocabulary to avoid: autonomy-first framing, LLM/model/architecture jargon, 'replace your staff'.
findings.evidence: Three primary-source verbatim confirmations (3-0 each); Salesforce verified via indexed snippets (medium, 3-0) with the caveat that partner vocabulary leads but NLP/ML terms appear as supporting explanation.

findings.claim: Case-study pattern: present proof as one-line named-customer metric pairs or three-metric stat cards, leading with a quantified outcome — not narrative case studies. Decagon: Duolingo 80% deflection, ClassPass 95% cost reduction, Hunter Douglas $1M revenue from AI-handled conversations, in an 'Instant ROI on the metrics that matter' grid. Relevance AI: Qualified '$7M pipeline in 6 months / 35+ agents / 10x output', Send Payments '40 hrs saved weekly', Zembl '30% increase in customer conversion'. For a young studio without named logos, the transferable unit is [business type] + [single operational metric] (hours saved weekly, response time, bookings handled).
findings.evidence: Both verified verbatim by live fetch 2026-07-03, unanimous votes. Even Decagon's testimonial carousel headlines the metric above the quote.

findings.claim: Conversion patterns among product companies: Decagon is purely demo-led ('Get a demo' everywhere, no self-serve, no assessment); Relevance AI runs a dual-CTA hero ('Talk to sales' + 'Try for free', no homepage pricing); Salesforce's SMB page converts via a gated e-book with a heavy multi-field form (name, email, phone, job title, company, employees, industry, country) plus free-trial CTAs — none of them offer a consultation or readiness assessment. This is the whitespace: an assessment-led path is differentiated against every product company studied, and its natural analog is the dual-CTA pattern with 'Start the free readiness check' as the low-friction option and 'Book a consultation' as the direct option.
findings.evidence: All three verified against primary pages 2026-07-03 with explicit negative checks (grep for demo/consult/assessment on Salesforce found no consultation offer; Decagon homepage has no signup or quiz).

findings.claim: Section order used to sell agents to SMBs (Salesforce template): question-form headline ('What Is an AI Agent For Small Business?') → plain definition → benefits (efficiency, cost, customer service, decision-making, scaling) → key-features checklist → product spotlight → industry use-case examples → challenges-and-solutions objection handling → future outlook → gated lead magnet → tiered CTA. The notable moves to borrow: a question-form H1 that meets buyers at their level of understanding, benefits before features, industry-specific examples, and an explicit objection-handling section.
findings.evidence: Full heading order extracted from the live canonical page 2026-07-03; every claimed section confirmed including the gated e-book form and tiered product CTA. Single page, so it is one vendor's template rather than an industry standard.

findings.claim: 'Hyperagents' is not an SMB agency: it is Torq HyperAgents(TM), an enterprise security vendor's trademarked custom-agent product ('Bespoke AI Agents that can drive any security process', demo-led CTAs). Adversarial search found no SMB agency by that name (the only other exact-name entity is a Meta research framework). The name is therefore not a competitive threat in the SMB studio space, but note the pattern it demonstrates: trademarked product name + one-line capability subheadline, and 'bespoke AI agents' as buyer-friendly phrasing for custom agent work.
findings.evidence: H1 and subheadline verified verbatim by live fetch 2026-07-03; 2-1 vote with the minor qualification that Torq is not the sole user of the string.

findings.claim: Readiness-assessment dimensions (what to score): Cisco's AI Readiness Index uses six weighted pillars — Strategy 15%, Infrastructure 25%, Data 20%, Governance 15%, Talent 15%, Culture 10% — across 49 indicators; BridgeView IT's SMB-specific quiz compresses to five pillars: data maturity, team enablement, technology infrastructure, strategic alignment, governance & risk. The overlap defines the canonical dimension set; for agent-readiness specifically, 'infrastructure' translates to existing tools/channels and 'strategy' to having an owner and identified repetitive processes.
findings.evidence: Cisco methodology confirmed via indexed primary page and 2025 edition (weights corroborated across Cisco documents); BridgeView five pillars confirmed near-verbatim via indexed page and Wayback capture. Both unanimous.

findings.claim: Scoring mechanics and tier labels: Cisco scores each indicator by deployment maturity, not yes/no — Full Deployment 100%, Partial 25-50%, None 0% — and labels four tiers with explicit cutoffs: Pacesetters (>=86, Fully Prepared), Chasers (61-85, Moderately Prepared), Followers (31-60, Limited Preparedness), Laggards (0-30, Unprepared). BridgeView, by contrast, deliberately avoids tier labels for SMBs, delivering a custom score + executive summary of strengths + next-step recommendations. Recommended hybrid for a studio quiz: graded (never binary) answer options, four tiers with encouraging SMB-friendly names (e.g. Agent-Ready >=80, Nearly Ready 55-79, Building the Foundation 30-54, Start With the Basics <30), and a strengths-first report framing per BridgeView so low scorers still book a call.
findings.evidence: Cisco tier cutoffs and 0/25-50/100 scoring verified verbatim (Wayback capture of methodology page, 2025-m11 edition; independently corroborated by third-party article). BridgeView's no-tier, three-deliverable output verified against 2026-04-15 Wayback capture (2-1 on that sub-claim). All others unanimous.

findings.claim: Recommended 7-question agent-readiness quiz (synthesized from Cisco's weighted-pillar + graded-maturity model and BridgeView's SMB pillar set), each question answered on a 3-level scale scored 0 / 1 / 2 (mirroring Cisco's none/partial/full): (1) Process documentation — 'If a key staff member left tomorrow, could someone follow written steps to do their job?' (weight 20%); (2) Data digitization — 'Where do your records (bookings, sales, inventory) live: paper, spreadsheets/apps, or connected software?' (weight 20%); (3) Repetitive-task volume — 'How many hours per week does your team spend on the same repeated tasks (replying to enquiries, taking bookings, chasing payments)?' (weight 20%); (4) Existing tools/channels — 'Do you already run the business on digital channels (WhatsApp Business, POS, accounting app)?' (weight 15%); (5) Staff structure/ownership — 'Is there one person who could own and check an AI agent's work weekly?' (weight 10%); (6) Strategic clarity — 'Can you name the one process that, if automated, would most change your business?' (weight 10%); (7) Risk tolerance/governance — 'Are you comfortable letting a system draft replies that a human approves before sending?' (weight 5%). The three heaviest weights track Cisco's finding that data and infrastructure dominate readiness; questions 1-3 are the strongest predictors for operations businesses (farms, venues) because agents automate documented, digitized, repetitive work.
findings.evidence: This is a synthesis recommendation: dimensions, graded scoring, and weighting logic are directly grounded in verified Cisco/BridgeView frameworks (all 3-0), but the specific question wording, weights, and their predictive claim are the researcher's design, not independently validated.

findings.claim: Assessment-led conversion copy and journey (BridgeView template, directly reusable): lead with speed and low friction — 'Get clarity on your AI Strategy in just 5 minutes', CTA 'Start Your Assessment Now', reassurance line 'No technical prep required' — then a 3-step how-it-works (complete assessment in under 10 minutes → instant personalized report → roadmap), a closing 'Schedule a Consultation' CTA, and an FAQ that explicitly upsells from assessment to strategic planning, vendor sourcing, or full implementation. The whole page sells the assessment, not the service; the service is sold by the report and the FAQ.
findings.evidence: All copy verified verbatim against the 2026-04-15 Wayback capture with current search-index corroboration; unanimous votes on hero copy and journey structure. Minor on-page inconsistency: hero promises 5 minutes, how-it-works says under 10.

findings.claim: Quiz vs contact form evidence: Interact's platform data shows service-provider businesses (the closest category to an agent studio selling consultations) convert 42.2% of quiz starters into leads, with 47.3% start-to-finish completion. This supports assessment-led conversion, but two claims commonly made alongside it were refuted in verification: the '40.1% average vs 2-5% contact forms' comparison and the '65% completion since 2013' figure did not survive. Cite only the service-provider figure, attribute it to Interact's own (unaudited, vendor) platform data, and note the denominator is quiz starts, not page visitors.
findings.evidence: 42.2%/47.3% verified verbatim against the report (updated Dec 2025) and directionally corroborated by ScoreApp (38.5% B2B professional services) and KyLeads (30-40%); 2-1 vote; vendor-reported with no disclosed methodology.

findings.claim: African/Nigerian market shift: Meta announced the Meta Business Agent at Conversations 2026 (June 2026) — an AI assistant built into WhatsApp Business handling customer conversations 24/7, available worldwide at no cost at launch with no business-size requirements (paid subscription tiers planned in coming months). A WhatsApp-first agent studio in Africa therefore now competes with a free platform-native incumbent for basic chat automation. The defensible positioning is above the Meta layer: multi-step operational agents wired into the business's actual processes (bookings, inventory, farm operations, payments) — 'agent as a system', which Meta's generic reply-bot does not do.
findings.evidence: 3-0 vote; corroborated by Meta's own WhatsApp Business blog and TechCrunch (2026-06-03, global rollout after ~2 years testing in India and Mexico). The positioning implication is a reasonable inference flagged as such by verifiers.

findings.claim: Recommended page section order for a consultation-led journey (synthesis of Decagon/Relevance hero patterns, Salesforce SMB section order, and BridgeView assessment flow): (1) Hero — metaphor/outcome headline + human-control clause + dual CTA ('Start the 5-minute readiness check' primary, 'Book a consultation' secondary); (2) Plain-language 'What is an AI agent?' using partner/playbook vocabulary with a question-form heading; (3) Benefits in SMB terms (time saved, cost, customers answered 24/7, owner visibility); (4) Industry use cases — farm, venue/hospitality, services — each as a mini-scenario with one quantified metric; (5) How it works — 3 steps: take the assessment → instant scored report → roadmap call; (6) Proof — metric-led stat cards (named customers when available, anonymized business types until then); (7) Objection handling / FAQ including 'what happens after the assessment' upsell; (8) Readiness quiz section (or persistent CTA); (9) Closing consultation CTA. Keep the quiz form minimal — Salesforce's 8-field gate is an enterprise pattern; BridgeView's low-friction promise fits SMBs better.
findings.evidence: Synthesis recommendation: every component pattern is verified against a primary source (all 3-0), but the combined ordering is the researcher's design and has not been A/B validated.

result.caveats: Three key caveats. (1) Conversion evidence is the weakest link: the Interact 42.2% figure is vendor-reported platform data with no disclosed methodology, its denominator is quiz starts (not page visitors), and the two broader quiz-vs-form comparison claims (40.1% average vs 2-5% contact forms; 65% completion) were refuted in verification — so the case for assessment-led conversion rests on one medium-confidence benchmark plus the observed practice of consultancies, not controlled studies. (2) The African/Nigerian SMB messaging-gap question is only partially answered: the widely-cited WhatsApp adoption statistics (78% of Sub-Saharan SMBs, 52M Nigerian downloads) were refuted, and no verified source covered how agentic AI is currently marketed to Nigerian farms or hospitality venues specifically — the gap is inferred from absence of evidence, not documented. (3) Time-sensitivity: Meta's Business Agent is free 'at launch' (June 2026) with paid tiers explicitly planned within months, so the competitive framing will shift; all homepage copy was verified live on 2026-07-03 and marketing pages change frequently. Additionally, the recommended quiz weights and page order are synthesized designs grounded in verified frameworks (Cisco, BridgeView) but not independently validated, and several sources (Cisco, Salesforce, BridgeView) were bot-blocked and verified via Wayback captures or indexed snippets rather than live fetches.
openQuestions: How is agentic AI actually being marketed to Nigerian/African SMBs today (local agencies, pricing norms, channel mix), and what verified WhatsApp adoption data exists for Nigerian SMBs? The strongest local-market claims were refuted, leaving this largely unanswered.

What will Meta Business Agent's paid tiers cost and what capabilities will they include — and does it (or will it) support multi-step operational workflows that would encroach on the 'agent as a system' positioning?

What is the visitor-to-quiz-start rate for assessment lead magnets (all verified benchmarks start the funnel at quiz start), and how do assessment-sourced leads compare on close rate and deal size versus demo-request leads for B2B services?

How do the named agent companies (LangChain, CrewAI, Lindy, Sierra AI, Cognition/Devin) that were in scope but produced no surviving claims position themselves — particularly Sierra and Lindy, whose SMB-adjacent messaging would be most comparable?

refuted.claim: Quizzes convert 40.1% of starters into leads on average, according to Interact's platform data — far above typical B2B contact form conversion benchmarks (commonly cited at 2-5%), supporting assessment-led conversion over plain contact forms.
65% of people who start a quiz complete all questions, a rate the report says has held roughly steady since 2013 across more than 80 million leads generated on the platform.

78% of small businesses in Sub-Saharan Africa already use WhatsApp as their main sales channel, and the WhatsApp Business app has been downloaded 52.47 million times in Nigeria — the highest in Africa and second only to India worldwide — establishing WhatsApp as the default channel any agent product for Nigerian SMBs must meet customers on.
